sections.overview: The inventory name Megaphobema mesomelas is an older combination; the World Spider Catalog accepts Abdomegaphobema mesomelas, a Costa Rican tarantula.
sections.identification: The World Spider Catalog confirms the accepted species and its Costa Rican distribution; the common name refers to the contrasting reddish legs.
sections.habitat: A Costa Rican natural-history record describes it from forested areas and burrows in holes made by other animals or dug into vertical banks.
sections.diet: It is a predator of small animals; a study from Monteverde examined its prey choices and found that prey type and abundance did not alone predict preference.
sections.behavior: It is a burrowing, ground-dwelling tarantula; observations outside the burrow are reported during the breeding season.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific breeding details remain poorly documented in the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: As a ground predator, it feeds on other animals and is part of the forest-floor food web.
sections.conservation: The World Spider Catalog records the species in Costa Rica but does not assign a conservation category.
